# Answer

The leftmost road vehicle in the image is the red truck parked immediately to the east of the yellow house with the red roof at the top-left of the diorama.
The rightmost road vehicle in the image is the small yellow car on the south-east road, just south-east of the large steel electricity pylon on the right side of the image.

The shortest drivable road route from the yellow-car position to the red-truck position requires **3 complete turns**.

In chronological order the turns are:

1. **A U-turn.** The yellow car is standing on the south-east road facing south-east, away from the rest of the road network, and that road ends to the south-east. It must therefore turn completely around to head north-west up the same road toward the main central junction by the small red-roof signal house, where the white van and the blue pick-up with white tanks are standing.

2. **A right turn.** At that central junction, with the car now heading north-west, it must turn right to the north / north-east onto the diagonal grey road that leads north across the double-track railway level-crossing, past the red flat-bed truck, to the upper yard road at the top-centre by the small brown building.

3. **A left turn.** After crossing the railway to the north, with the car now heading north, it must turn left to the west onto the upper yard road that runs north of the tracks, and then follow that road west past the white building and the large silo to the parking area behind the yellow house, which is the position of the red truck.

Following curves in a single road, for example the bend of the main road or the bend of the south-east road, requires only minor steering adjustments and is not counted as a complete turn. No other complete left, right or U-turn is needed on this shortest route.
